title: A-trade grading — non-blocking review follow-ups
description: Non-blocking findings from pr-reviewer's review of PR #149 (backend-trade-grading), tracked here per CLAUDE.md's autonomous-pipeline rule so they aren't lost once that PR merges.

checklist.step: GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades shares the per-ticker daily-history fetch across a ticker's rows (`_grade_closed_trades`'s `frames` dict), but the more expensive per-ticker derivation inside `grade_closed_trade` -- `drop_malformed_daily_bars(daily_ohlcv)` and the full `autoenvelope()` rolling-window computation over the whole history -- is redundantly recomputed once per closed-trade row instead of once per ticker. A ticker with many round-trip closed trades (e.g. 50 AAPL buy/sell pairs) triggers 50 separate dropna passes and 50 separate autoenvelope() computations over the identical frame, growing linearly with trade count per ticker rather than being computed once and reused. Fix by precomputing the filtered frame + channel once per ticker in `_grade_closed_trades` and passing the already-derived entry/exit rows + channel bounds into `grade_trade` directly, bypassing `grade_closed_trade`'s per-call re-derivation for the multi-row-per-ticker case.

decisions.decision: Instead of extracting entry/exit rows + bare channel-bound floats in `_grade_closed_trades` and calling `grade_trade` directly (the checklist's literal phrasing), added a new `app.portfolio.grading.grade_trade_from_filtered_history(*, entry_price, entry_date, exit_price, exit_date, filtered_daily_ohlcv, channel)` that takes the already-filtered frame + already-computed channel DataFrame and does the entry/exit-date row lookup (including the not-an-exact-row -> all-None degrade) itself; `_grade_closed_trades` calls this once per row after computing `filtered_daily_ohlcv`/`channel` once per ticker, and `grade_closed_trade` (the single-trade convenience wrapper, kept for its own existing unit tests and as the correct entry point for grading one trade in isolation) now derives those two and delegates to it too.
decisions.rationale: The row-lookup-and-degrade-to-None logic (`entry_ts`/`exit_ts` not in the filtered frame's index -> an all-None TradeGrade) is exactly the kind of per-row derivation this followup is about sharing, not duplicating -- inlining it into the router's `_grade_closed_trades` (to match the checklist's literal 'passing entry/exit rows + channel bounds into grade_trade directly' wording) would have duplicated that not-a-trivial-one-liner degrade check in two places (router and grading.py) and made it easy for the two to drift. Keeping it as one grading.py function callable either once (via grade_closed_trade, single trade) or in a loop over a shared filtered_daily_ohlcv/channel pair (via _grade_closed_trades, many trades on one ticker) achieves the exact same fix -- the expensive dropna/autoenvelope passes happen once per ticker, not once per row -- while keeping the pure-domain-function-plus-thin-router-glue split the original backend-trade-grading task's own decisions established (grading logic lives in app.portfolio.grading, not app.api.routers.portfolio). Verified byte-identical output between the two call paths with a dedicated unit test (TestGradeTradeFromFilteredHistory.test_grade_closed_trade_delegates_to_it_with_identical_results) and added an integration test (TestGetClosedTradesSharesOneFetchPerTicker.test_two_trades_same_ticker_only_filter_and_channel_once) that monkeypatches drop_malformed_daily_bars/autoenvelope in the router module to assert each is called exactly once for two same-ticker closed trades, not the pre-fix once-per-row.

comments.summary: The checklist's literal phrasing (pass entry/exit rows + channel bounds directly into grade_trade) was deviated from in favor of a new grade_trade_from_filtered_history(filtered_daily_ohlcv, channel) that does its own row lookup/degrade-to-None. Verified reasonable: avoids duplicating the not-in-index -> all-None degrade logic across router and grading.py, keeps the pure-domain-function/thin-router-glue split the original backend-trade-grading task established, and is fully documented in this task's own decisions entry.

Byte-identical-output claim (TestGradeTradeFromFilteredHistory.test_grade_closed_trade_delegates_to_it_with_identical_results) verified genuine: grade_closed_trade and grade_trade_from_filtered_history produce identical TradeGrade for the same inputs, confirmed by running the actual test.

Integration test TestGetClosedTradesSharesOneFetchPerTicker.test_two_trades_same_ticker_only_filter_and_channel_once genuinely catches a regression back to per-row drop_malformed_daily_bars/autoenvelope recomputation. Verified experimentally by reverting _grade_closed_trades to the pre-fix per-row grade_closed_trade call and re-running: the test fails (dropna_calls/autoenvelope_calls read 0, not the expected 1) rather than passing silently. See backend-trade-grading-followups-followups for a minor non-blocking note on the exact failure-mode wording.

backend/openapi.json's diff is confirmed docstring-text-only (operationId, schema, response shapes all unchanged) -- re-ran scripts/export_openapi.py from a clean checkout and it produced zero diff against the committed snapshot. No frontend files are touched by this PR and none needed regeneration (frontend/src/api/types.ts's shape is unaffected by a description-only change).

Minor: the integration test's docstring and this task's own decision-entry rationale describe the regression as producing the pre-fix 'once-per-row' call count (implying 2), but the monkeypatch actually intercepts the router module's own name binding, which the pre-fix code path never called through at all -- the counters would read 0, not 2, on a revert. Test still correctly fails either way; tracked as a non-blocking wording fix in backend-trade-grading-followups-followups.

review.notes: Full review: backend suite 807 passed, 99.92% coverage (90% gate met); ruff/mypy clean; frontend unchanged by this PR (lint re-run clean as a baseline sanity check, tsc/vitest skipped as genuinely not applicable -- no frontend files in the diff). code-review skill (medium effort, background) found zero issues. verify-elder-signal: grade_trade/buy_grade_pct/sell_grade_pct/trade_grade_pct (the actual Elder ch. 55 formulas) are untouched by this diff -- confirmed via diff inspection; only the wrapper/data-plumbing structure changed, autoenvelope() is still invoked with the same filtered-frame['close'] input and drop_malformed_daily_bars still defaults to require_full_ohlc_on_latest_bar=True, so no methodology drift. No new module/dependency/layer added (architecture-review not applicable). No frontend components touched (placement check not applicable). UI-facing check: this PR touches GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades, which has a frontend consumer (TradeJournalPanel) -- ran the persisted e2e suite (make e2e, all 16 specs passed including real hits to GET /api/portfolio/closed-trades returning 200 in a real browser) as the closest available substitute for an interactive Playwright MCP walkthrough, since no browser MCP tool was available in this review session's toolset; the change is a pure backend performance refactor with byte-identical output verified by dedicated unit/integration tests, so this is judged sufficient. One non-blocking wording-accuracy finding filed as backend-trade-grading-followups-followups.
